all 3 .acx-incoming sidecars resolved keep-local: the incoming current_state.md is a 3.4KB blank template vs 34KB of real state; systematic-debugging drift is sanctioned because those files are manifest tier scaffold
a PASS delta is not improvement when the validator itself grew: validate.sh gained 273 lines, so 89->107 PASS is new checks, not newly passing old ones
a simulated exit settles at the price an ORDER could have received, never a bar intraday extreme - high/low answer WHICH barrier was touched, not at what price the position left
settlement must stay clamped inside [low, high]: the old code was bounded by construction because it WAS the high or low, so introducing the open created a new unbounded path
a metric with undefined dispersion reports None not 0.0 - std() of a single pick is NaN and the old guard fabricated a zero the UI styled as a real result
two PRE-EXISTING tests were pinning the defect (actual_return == -0.1 = session low) - a suite can actively defend a bug, so check what the old assertions encode before trusting them
gap-up-through-target on a stop bar deferred on MEASURED grounds: only 4 of 99287 real bars have the >=20% intraday range it needs, and TW +-10% price limit makes it near-impossible
an embargo is a statement about TIME not rows - on a stacked panel one date is N rows, so the two are equivalent only when N=1, which is why the bug survived
degrade diagnostics, never the guarantee - the CV loop is informational so it degrades 3->2->skipped, while the holdout embargo aborts when it cannot be honoured
a history entry LACKING an embargo key is a pre-fix marker by construction - never backfill it onto old entries
measure the cliff before claiming safety: the binding constraint was ~4x PRED_DAYS distinct TRAINING DATES and was independent of ticker count, not the 22-date floor I had checked
an abort must be visible to callers - returning None on both success and refusal let a scheduled retrain report success with no model written
writing a truthfulness spec does not make your own prose true - the fact-check brief caught 3 errors in text written DURING this feature, including a sentence the cited test file itself falsifies
a claim sheet must cite the code implementing each row, and a row whose implementation is removed becomes a stated limitation rather than a quiet deletion
send a machine token through the API and keep the display label at the presentation layer - string matching on user-facing wording is a silent-failure mode
fixing the target lines is not enough: the same claim survived in README, the highest-traffic file, which is where the next auditor greps first
survivorship bias is NOT mitigated by random sampling - sampling from a survivor-only universe is unbiased WITHIN survivors and says nothing about the names that left
precision is unreadable without its base rate - report lift over the TEST-split prevalence, and 1.0 is not a tunable threshold but the base rate by definition
a health check must fail TOWARD disclosure: NaN and inf slipped through both guards because nan <= 1.0 is False and nan is None is False
changing behaviour without touching the display layer is how a chip ends up asserting a fact the panel beneath it contradicts - a status with several causes needs a machine reason
never borrow another entry when the active version is missing from history - a vague status could survive it, a specific numeric claim cannot
a test that cannot fail is worse than no test: two rounds of theatre here, one caught by me and one by the reviewer
an irreversible action requires a comparable measurement - where one is unavailable the action does not happen, and unrankable means PROTECTED rather than sorted last
deletion must be an ALLOW-LIST, never everything-not-kept: history is truncated, so a keep-set silently stops covering older files and the protection expired at ~50 entries
a claim a spec cannot deliver gets removed with the derivation, not reworded - no benchmark window is out-of-sample under a full-data refit
a test that duplicates the logic it tests can only confirm the duplicate - three separate sets of tests in this epic defended the bugs they were meant to catch
the entry-to-filename mapping is where protection leaks: minute-resolution timestamps mean two history entries can name the same .pkl
rows are not time - a row offset used where a date was meant is correct only when every series has the same length, the same mistake as the training embargo in a different file
a disclosure field that undercounts is worse than silence: counting one exclusion cause out of three made a 16-of-300 cross-section report 0 excluded
a marker read from a key the real data does not have is a hard-wired constant - and the test passed because it mocked a shape the file never has
measure against real data, not just fixtures: a head-slice pre-pass passed every unit test and returned zero picks on the real DB because all 25 sampled candidates were empty
an order-dependent test is worse than a failing one - it reports a pass that depends on what else ran
